title: Assembly and Operation of an Acoustofluidic Device for Enhanced Delivery of Molecular Compounds to Cells
protocol: Obtain a photomask with a concentric spiral design containing channels with a diameter of 500 µm.
Prepare a mold of the concentric spiral design on a photoresist-coated silicon wafer using standard photolithography techniques.
Add approximately 2 Tbsp (~30 mL) of SU-8 2100 to a 100 mm silicon wafer.
Spin-coat the wafer at 150 rpm for 30 s, then increase speed to 1,200 rpm for 60 s to yield a thickness of 200 µm.
Cure the photoresist-coated wafer in a polyimide vacuum oven with a 30 min ramp up and 30 min dwell at 115 °C, then ramp down for 30 min.
Expose the photoresist-coated wafer for 130 s using a mask aligner with the photomask from step 1.1.
Bake the wafer after exposure following the same process described in step 1.2.3.
Develop the photoresist in SU-8 developer solution for approximately 8 min.
Silanize the mold to make the surface more hydrophobic.
Place the photoresist-coated wafer into a desiccator.
Add a 20 µL drop of chlorosilane (C8H4Cl3F13Si) to the desiccator.
Apply vacuum to the chamber for 30 seconds.
Seal the chamber and leave overnight.
Combine 54 g of polydimethsiloxane (PDMS) base with 6 g of curing agent in a cup.
Mix vigorously and thoroughly with a spatula for at least 1 minute.
Place the cup containing the PDMS solution into a desiccator for approximately 30 minutes or until remnant air bubbles are removed from the solution.
Place photoresist-coated wafer with the patterns facing upward in a 150-mm Petri dish.
Pour the PDMS solution over the mold inside the 150-mm Petri dish.
If needed, place the 150-mm Petri dish inside a desiccator and apply vacuum until remnant air bubbles disappear.
Transfer the 150-mm Petri dish into a lab oven and bake for 2 hours at 60 °C to cure the PDMS.
After curing, carefully remove the PDMS from the Petri dish by cutting around the edges of the wafer using a razor blade.
Cut out each individual device using a knife or razor blade.
Punch holes through the inlet and outlet ports of each device using a 2.5-mm biopsy punch.
Place each PDMS device in a plasma asher with channels exposed facing upward.
Apply oxygen plasma treatment at 100 W for 45 seconds and 500 mbar O2 pressure.
Immediately place each treated PDMS device onto a clean soda lime glass microscope slide, with channels facing the glass surface.
Let devices bond overnight at room temperature.
Gently apply silicone to the surface of the 1-cm diameter piezo transducer to a thickness of ~1-2mm.
Carefully align the transducer with the concentric spiral and gently press it onto the bottom of the glass microscope slide (opposite side from the PDMS device).
Connect a microcontroller to a computer using a USB A to B cable.
Upload an 8 MHz signal generating program to the microcontroller via the associated program on the computer.
Solder a 1" 22G wire to the end of each wire on the PZT transducer.
Connect the negative (black) terminal wire of PZT transducer to a GND pin via the soldered wire.
Connect the positive (red) terminal wire of PZT transducer to the output pin (#9 in the provided example program) via the soldered wire.
Mount the acoustofluidic device and the microcontroller in a 3D-printed case.
Cut 3-6" sections of tygon PVC soft plastic tubing (1/16" ID, 1/8" OD).
Push the tubing into the inlet and outlet ports.
Rotate the tubing while applying pressure to fit it in the opening.
Apply glue at the junction to bond the PDMS and tubing together if desired.
Assemble the microfluidic reservoir according to manufacturer's instructions.
Cut a 3-6" section of tygon PVC soft plastic tubing (1/16" ID, 1/8" OD).
Push the tubing over the 1/32" ID tubing from the microfluidic reservoir output tubing.
Wrap the junction with paraffin film to prevent leakage if desired.
Fill a 60-mL syringe with ambient air.
Optionally, filter the air through a 0.2-µm filter.
Connect the syringe to tygon PVC tubing on the side of the microfluidic reservoir.
Set the syringe pump to a rate of 200 mL/h.
Push cell/ultrasound contrast agent solutions through the acoustofluidic device at a volumetric flow rate of 50 mL/h.
Collect samples from the output of the acoustofluidic device into a 50mL centrifuge tube.
Optionally, rinse channel prior to treatment with 15 mL of 70% ethanol solution to increase sterility of fluidic channels.
Rinse channels with 15 mL of deionized water to remove residual ethanol in the device prior to pumping cells through the system.
Prepare a phospholipid solution in a 20mL scintillation vial.
Add 25 mg of 1,2-distearoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (DSPC).
Add 11.6 mg of 1,2-distearoyl-sn-glycero-3-ethylphosphocholine (DSEPC).
Add 0.26 mg of 1,2-distearoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoglycerol (DSPG).
Add 0.88 mg of polyoxyethylene40 stearate.
Add chloroform until all phospholipids are dissolved (e.g., 3 mL of chloroform).
Evaporate chloroform in a desiccator for 48 h to form a dry lipid film.
Rehydrate the lipid film with 10 mL of sterile phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Sonicate the lipid solution for 3 min at 40% amplitude to form a cationic micellar solution.
Store the phospholipid solution at 2-6 °C for up to 1 month.
Add 200 µL of cationic micellar solution and 600 µL of sterile PBS to a 2 mL glass septum vial.
Seal the vial by crimping the cap.
Fill the vial head space with decafluorobutane gas for 30 s using a 1.5" 20G needle.
Amalgamate the vial for 45 s at 4,350 cpm to form perfluorobutane gas-filled ultrasound contrast agents.
Add 25 µL of ultrasound contrast agent solution per 1 mL of cell solution immediately before pumping through the acoustofluidic device.
Isolate peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from whole blood solutions and store at -150 °C.
Thaw frozen vial in 37 °C water bath.
Dilute thawed PBMCs with PBS at a 1:10 ratio in a 15mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge diluted PBMCs at 580 x g for 11 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 13 mL of MACs running buffer.
Count the PBMCs using an automated cell counter or hemocytometer.
Centrifuge the PBMCs again at 580 x g for 11 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and add 40 µL of chilled running buffer per 10 million PBMCs.
Add 10 µL of Pan T-Cell Biotin Antibody Cocktail per 10 million PBMCs to isolate T cells.
Gently agitate the solution and store it at 4°C for 5 minutes per 10 million cells.
Add 30 µL of running buffer and 20 µL of Pan T-Cell MicroBead Cocktail per 10 million PBMCs.
Mix thoroughly and incubate for an additional 15 minutes at 4°C.
Separate primary T cells using a commercially available benchtop magnetic sorting instrument following the manufacturer's protocol.
Count T cells using an automated cell counter or hemocytometer.
Dilute T cells in 10 mL of sterile PBS and centrifuge at 580 x g for 10 minutes at 4°C to pellet the cells.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend T cells in 1 mL of PBS.
Count T cells using an automated cell counter or hemocytometer again.
Aliquot T cells at a concentration of 1 million/mL for experiments.
Prepare a 1 mg/mL fluorescein solution in PBS.
Add 100 µL of 1 mg/mL fluorescein solution per 1 mL of T cell solution immediately prior to processing.
Add 25 µL of ultrasound contrast agent solution as previously described in step 3.11.
Process 1 mL aliquots of cells using the acoustofluidic system (see steps 2.10-2.11).
Wash cells three times via centrifugation at 580 x g for 10 min with 500 µL of PBS to remove extracellular fluorescein.
Resuspend cells in 250 µL of PBS and measure fluorescence on flow cytometer after final washing step.
Culture A549 (adenocarcinomic human alveolar basal epithelial) cells in complete DMEM media at 37 °C and 5% CO2 in a flat-bottom tissue culture flask.
Harvest A549 cells when they reach 70-90% confluency.
Aspirate media from the flask and wash the cells once with PBS to remove serum proteins.
Add trypsin (0.25%) EDTA to the flask and incubate for 5 min at 37 °C.
Transfer trypsin solution to a 15 mL centrifuge tube and neutralize it by adding complete DMEM media at a 1:3 ratio.
Pellet the cells via centrifugation at 1,500 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet at a concentration of 100,000/mL in PBS solution containing 200 mM trehalose in a 15-mL conical vial.
Add 25 µL of ultrasound contrast agent solution.
Process 1 mL aliquots of cells using the acoustofluidic system.
Wash cells three times via centrifugation with 500 µL of PBS to remove extracellular trehalose.
Resuspend cells in 100 µL of PBS after final washing step.
Add 11 µL of 1% Triton X-100 solution to lyse cells and release intracellular trehalose.
Vortex for 15 s, then incubate for 30 min at room temperature.
Vortex again for 15 s.
Measure trehalose concentration using a commercially available trehalose assay following the manufacturer's recommendation.
